title: The Conker

doing.t: is peeping out of its split, spiky case
has been polished by someone's thumb until it gleams
is threaded on a knotted string, ready for battle
has a pale, matt patch on top like a bald spot

close: Just the conker, turned so the grain swirls round it like polished wood.
Only the conker and its split green case, side by side.

roles.dark: for the deepest grain and the shadow beneath
roles.light: for the shine and the matt patch on top
roles.accent: for the green, spiky case

firstMark: Start with the shadow under the conker: a crescent of {dark}, pressed firmly.
Start with the swirl of grain in fine curved lines of {main}, leaving a bright window of paper for the shine.

title: The Fairy Ring

doing.t: has come up in an almost perfect circle
has one mushroom standing out of line
is made up of dozens of flat, fawn caps
has a gap where a few caps have toppled over

close: Just the fairy ring, seen from a little way above so the circle shows.
Only one mushroom from the ring, tipped up to show the gills underneath.

roles.dark: for the shadow under each cap
roles.light: for the creamy gills and stems
roles.accent: for the green of the grass

firstMark: Start with a faint ring of {main} dots to plan the circle before drawing any caps.
Start with the shadow tucked under the nearest cap in {dark}.

title: The Fly Agaric

doing.t: is still a round red button with its spots crowded together
has opened out flat and wide like a saucer
has had a corner of its cap nibbled
is wearing a frilled white skirt and leaning to one side

close: Just the toadstool, cap and stem, with all its white spots in place.
Only the fly agaric, seen from low down so the gills show under the rim.

roles.dark: for the shadow under the cap and the deepest red at the crown
roles.light: for the white spots and stem
roles.accent: for the orange where the red thins towards the rim

firstMark: Start with the spots: mark each one as a circle of bare paper, then colour around them in {main}.
Start with the dark band under the cap in {dark}, where the gills disappear into shade.

title: The Pinecone

doing.t: has opened every scale wide
has shut itself up tight as a fist
has a winged seed still caught between two scales
has had every tip dabbed with white paint

close: Just the pinecone, seen from the side so the scales spiral round.
Only the pinecone, from underneath, looking into the pattern of scales.

roles.dark: for the gaps between the scales
roles.light: for the worn lip of each scale
roles.accent: for the beads of amber resin

firstMark: Start with the dark gaps between the scales: small wedges of {dark}, working round from the bottom.
Start with the outline of one scale near the middle in {main}, then build outwards.

title: The Rosehips

doing.t: are hanging in a shiny cluster from a thorny stem
are each tipped with a dry brown tuft
have gone soft, dark and wrinkled
have one hip with a beak-sized peck taken out

close: Just the rosehips, three or four on one stem.
Only one rosehip, big enough to fill the page.

roles.dark: for the stems, the thorns and the shadow side of each hip
roles.light: for the glint on each hip
roles.accent: for the orange where the red is thinnest

firstMark: Start with the shine: draw an oval of bare paper on each hip and colour round it in {main}.
Start with the stem and its hooked thorns in {dark}, before any red goes down.

title: The Fern

doing.t: is unfurling one tight green coil
has its fronds spread out like long green feathers
is reaching out with one extra-long frond
has rows of brown dots along the backs of its fronds
has one frond turned the colour of toast

close: Just one frond of the fern, from the stalk to the tip.
Only the fiddlehead, coiled tight like the scroll of a violin.

roles.dark: for the stem and the shade between the leaflets
roles.light: for the new, yellowy green at the tips
roles.accent: for the brown dots on the backs of the fronds

firstMark: Start with the midrib of one frond: a single curved line of {dark} from base to tip.
Start with the coil at the tip in {main}, drawn like a snail shell.

title: The Striped Pebble
a: a pebble with a white stripe
the: the pebble with a white stripe
phrases: the stripe goes all the way round
cold, then warm in the hand

doing.t: is still wet and gleaming
sits at the top of a careful stack of three
has been chosen over a hundred plainer ones
is flecked with rust on either side of its stripe

close: Just the pebble, with the white stripe running round its middle like a ribbon.
Only the pebble, life size, with its speckles and the one clean stripe.

roles.dark: for the shadow it sits in
roles.light: for the white stripe and the shine
roles.accent: for the freckles of colour in the stone

firstMark: Start with the stripe: leave it as bare paper and colour each side of it in {main}.
Start with the shadow underneath, a flat oval of {dark} hugging the bottom edge.

title: The Sycamore Keys

doing.t: are still joined in pairs, wings spread wide
are hanging in a bunch from the end of a twig
are lying in a heap, waiting to be tossed up again
have come twirling down in a scatter
have dried from green to biscuit brown

close: Just one pair of sycamore keys, wings spread like a moth.
Only the sycamore keys, three pairs in a row, from green to brown.

roles.dark: for the seed at the base of each wing
roles.light: for the see-through edge of the wings
roles.accent: for the blush of red along the veins

firstMark: Start with the seed: a plump teardrop of {dark} at the root of each wing.
Start with the veins of the wing in fine lines of {main}, fanning out from the seed.

title: The Foxgloves

doing.t: are standing to attention in a tall row
have a bumblebee backing out of the lowest bell
are leaning together, top-heavy with flowers
have flowered right up to the last bud

close: Just one foxglove spire, from the lowest bell to the top bud.
Only one bell, big enough to see the speckles inside.

roles.dark: for the deep throats of the bells
roles.light: for the creamy insides
roles.accent: for the dark speckles and the green stem

firstMark: Start with the open mouth of the lowest bell, a dark curve of {dark}.
Start with the outline of the lowest bell in {main}, then hang the others above it, each one a touch smaller.

title: The Bramble
phrases: one for the bowl, one for you

doing.t: is hung with blackberries, some ripe and some still red
has one fat blackberry that everyone else has missed
is arching over in a long, thorny loop
has pale pink flowers and hard green berries on the same stem
has its leaves going plum and crimson at the edges

close: Just one bramble stem with three blackberries at different stages.
Only the blackberry, near enough to count the beads.

roles.dark: for the shadows between the beads
roles.light: for the glints on each bead
roles.accent: for the red unripe berries and the leaves

firstMark: Start with one blackberry: a cluster of circles in {main}, each with a pinprick of paper left for the shine.
Start with the thorns along the stem, hooked marks in {dark}.

title: The Snowdrops

doing.t: are nodding their heads in a huddle
have opened their outer petals wide like wings
have only just come up, still closed
are standing in an egg cup, three stems together

close: Just one snowdrop, near enough to see the green mark on the inner petals.
Only the snowdrops, a clump of five, from a worm's-eye view.

roles.main: for the petals and their cool shadows
roles.dark: for the stems and leaves where they cross
roles.light: for the white of the petals
roles.accent: for the green mark inside each flower

firstMark: Start with the shadow side of each petal, the lightest touch of {dark}, and let the paper be the white.
Start with the stem in {dark}, arching over at the top like a hook.

title: The Bluebells
phrases: a blue haze under the trees

doing.t: are drooping over at the top like shepherd's crooks
have a bee hanging upside down from one bell
are half open, more green than blue
have one stem bowed right over by the weight of its bells

close: Just three bluebell stems, each one bending over at the tip.
Only one bluebell flower, with its petals rolled back.

roles.dark: for the inside of each bell
roles.light: for the paler tips of the petals
roles.accent: for the long green leaves

firstMark: Start with the bend of the stem in {dark}, curving over at the top.
Start with the lowest bell, a small upside-down cup of {main}.

title: The Dandelion Clock

doing.t: is still a flawless white globe
has lost half its seeds already
is standing tall on a hollow stalk
has a few seeds drifting off from one side

close: Just the dandelion clock, a round cloud of seeds on a single stalk.
Only one seed, drawn large, with its parachute of fine hairs.

roles.main: for the silvery grey of the seed globe
roles.dark: for the packed seeds at the centre
roles.light: for the fine white parachutes
roles.accent: for the green stalk

firstMark: Start at the centre with a dome of dense dots in {dark}, where the seeds are packed together.
Start with the parachutes, fine strokes of {main} radiating out from the middle.

title: The Sunflower
phrases: as wide as a dinner plate

doing.t: is turned full face towards the light
has a ruff of yellow petals round a dark, seedy middle
is still half closed, its petals folded over the middle
is drooping on its neck, heavy with seed
has had half its seeds pinched by the birds

close: Just the sunflower head, face on, with the seeds spiralling out from the middle.
Only the sunflower head, seen from the side, with its petals and green ruff behind.

roles.dark: for the seedy centre
roles.light: for the petal tips where the light shines through
roles.accent: for the green sepals and the stalk

firstMark: Start with the centre: a big circle of {dark} dots laid down in spirals.
Start with one petal at the top in {main}, then work round like a clock face.

title: The Pumpkin

doing.t: is sitting squat and ribbed with a curly stalk
still has a twist of dry tendril hanging off it
has a face carved into it and a candle lit inside
is lined up with two smaller ones in order of size

close: Just the pumpkin, with the ribs curving round from the stalk.
Only the stalk and the top of the pumpkin, up close, with its corky ridges.

roles.dark: for the grooves between the ribs
roles.light: for the shine across the top of each rib
roles.accent: for the dry green-brown stalk

firstMark: Start with the grooves: curved lines of {dark} running from the stalk to the base.
Start with the rib at the front in {main}, pressing harder towards its edges so it rounds out.

title: The Acorn
phrases: a whole oak, folded up small

doing.t: is wearing its cup like a flat cap
has lost its cup, which lies beside it like a dropped hat
is still green and sleek, half in its cup
has split and sent out one pale root

close: Just the acorn in its knobbly cup, drawn twice life size.
Only the acorn and its cup, apart, side by side.

roles.dark: for the shadow in the cup and under the acorn
roles.light: for the gleam on the shell
roles.accent: for the green blush near the base

firstMark: Start with the cup: a row of overlapping scales in {dark}.
Start with the curve of the acorn's shoulder in {main}, leaving a long highlight bare.

title: The Oak Leaf
phrases: edges wavy as a pie crust

doing.t: is lying upside down with its veins standing proud
is curling up at the tips as it dries
is pressed flat between the pages of a book
has a round gall like a marble stuck to its underside
is going russet round the edges
is still clinging to its twig, crisp and brown

close: Just the oak leaf, every lobe and vein, life size.
Only the oak leaf, half green and half russet.

roles.dark: for the veins and the curled edges
roles.light: for the silvery underside
roles.accent: for the last of the green

firstMark: Start with the central vein, one firm line of {dark} from stalk to tip.
Start with the wavy outline in {main}, one lobe at a time.

title: The Holly

doing.t: is thick with red berries
has one leaf near the top with no prickles at all
has leaves so shiny they look varnished
has been tied with a bow of tartan ribbon

close: Just the sprig of holly, three leaves and a cluster of berries.
Only one holly leaf, with every prickle pointing its own way.

roles.dark: for the shadows where the leaves overlap
roles.light: for the hard white shine on each leaf
roles.accent: for the red berries

firstMark: Start with the centre vein of each leaf in {dark}, then draw the prickly edges out from it.
Start with the outline of the top leaf in {main}, zigzagging from point to point.

title: The Ivy

doing.t: is creeping along in a line of pointed leaves
has sent one long shoot off on its own
is spilling over the edge of its pot
is covered in round green flower heads, humming with insects
is hung with clusters of black berries

close: Just one length of ivy, five leaves and the stem that joins them.
Only one ivy leaf, with its pale veins left as bare paper.

roles.dark: for the deepest shade and the berries
roles.light: for the chalky veins
roles.accent: for the reddish stems

firstMark: Start with the veins of one leaf: leave them as bare paper and colour between them in {main}.
Start with the stem as a wandering line of {dark}, then hang the leaves off it.

title: The Mossy Stone

doing.t: is furred with moss on its shady side
has moss so deep you could press a thumb into it
has a snail asleep in a dip in the moss
has moss sprouting hair-thin stalks with brown tips

close: Just the mossy stone, with the moss drawn as hundreds of short strokes.
Only the top of the stone, where the moss is thickest.

roles.dark: for the shadow under the stone and down in the moss
roles.light: for the bright tips of the moss
roles.accent: for the grey stone where it shows through

firstMark: Start with the moss in stippled dots of {main}, crowded together where it grows thickest.
Start with the shadow at the base in {dark}, then work up the stone.

title: The Lichen Twig
phrases: only where the air is clean

doing.t: is frilled all over with sage-green lichen
has a spot of orange lichen like a crumb of marmalade
forks into a perfect Y
has a single bud still waiting at its tip

close: Just the twig, with the lichen built up in crinkled layers.
Only the end of the twig, where the lichen ruffles like lettuce.

roles.dark: for the twig and the gaps under the frills
roles.light: for the lightest edges of the frills
roles.accent: for the spot of orange

firstMark: Start with the twig in {dark}, a slightly crooked line with a fork near the end.
Start with the frilly edge of one patch of lichen in {main}, like the edge of a cabbage leaf.

title: The Bird's Nest
phrases: a cup made with a beak
moss, hair and a bit of string

doing.t: is woven from moss, grass and one stray thread of red wool
is lined with a few downy feathers
is holding four blue-green eggs
is full of open yellow beaks
has been left empty, its lining pressed flat

close: Just the nest, looking down into the cup.
Only the nest, from the side, the strands wound round and round.

roles.dark: for the hollow inside the cup
roles.light: for the straw-coloured stalks on top
roles.accent: for the stray thread of wool

firstMark: Start with the dark hollow of the cup, an oval of {dark} pressed in firmly.
Start with the rim in short, curved strokes of {main}, going round and round.

title: The Speckled Egg

doing.t: is lying in a nest beside three others
has a hairline crack and a beak tip showing
is tucked under the edge of a downy feather

close: Just the egg, life size, with each freckle placed one at a time.
Only the egg and the edge of the nest around it.

roles.dark: for the shadow side of the egg
roles.light: for the highlight on the curve
roles.accent: for the rusty freckles

firstMark: Start with the shadow on the egg's underside, a gentle crescent of {dark}.
Start with an even, light layer of {main}, leaving an oval of paper near the top for the shine.

title: The Jay Feather
phrases: the bluest thing in the wood

doing.t: has its blue bars catching the light
is tucked into the band of an old straw hat
has a ruffled edge where the barbs have come apart
is standing upright in a jam jar of finds
is drifting down in slow loops

close: Just the feather, life size, with the bars counted carefully.
Only the barred blue part of the feather, drawn as large as the page allows.

roles.dark: for the black stripes between them
roles.light: for the white bands and the shaft
roles.accent: for the fluffy brown base

firstMark: Start with the shaft, one fine curved line of {dark} from base to tip.
Start with the blue bar nearest the tip in {main}, then leave a gap for the white before the next.

title: The Whelk Shell

doing.t: is spiralled tight, its point worn blunt
is lying mouth up, still gritty with sand
has a barnacle or two stuck to its back
is propped on its side so the spiral shows

close: Just the shell, turned so the spiral winds up to its point.
Only the opening of the shell, pearly and pinkish, turning inwards.

roles.dark: for the inside of the opening and the grooves of the spiral
roles.light: for the smooth lip
roles.accent: for the peachy pink inside

firstMark: Start with the opening: a dark curl of {dark} where the shell turns inwards.
Start with the spiral line in {main}, from the point down, getting wider as it goes.

title: The Cockle Shell

doing.t: is open like a butterfly, still joined at the hinge
has a neat round hole worn near its hinge
is holding a thimbleful of water
is one of a row of shells set out by size

close: Just the cockle shell, its ribs running out from the hinge.
Only the inside of the shell, smooth and pale, with the ribs showing through at the rim.

roles.dark: for the grooves between the ribs
roles.light: for the smooth inside
roles.accent: for the rusty bands of colour

firstMark: Start at the hinge and draw the ribs out like a fan in {main}.
Start with the grooves in fine lines of {dark}, each one fanning out from the hinge.

title: The Sea Glass

doing.t: is worn smooth and frosted all over
is glowing green with the light behind it
is shaped almost exactly like a heart
sits in a saucer with a handful of blue and white ones

close: Just the sea glass, its frosted surface built up in light, circling strokes.
Only the sea glass, brightest at the edges where it is thinnest.

roles.dark: for the deeper green at the thick edges
roles.light: for the milky frosting
roles.accent: for the cast shadow, tinted green

firstMark: Start with the thick edge, where the colour is deepest, in {dark}.
Start with an even, light layer of {main} in small circles, so the glass looks frosted rather than shiny.

title: The Driftwood
phrases: a long way from its tree

doing.t: is bleached silver and smooth as a bone
is worn into the shape of a sleeping dog
has a knot hole worn right through
still has a length of blue rope knotted round one end
has three pebbles balanced along its top

close: Just the driftwood, with the grain drawn in long, flowing lines.
Only the knotted end of the driftwood, up close.

roles.dark: for the cracks and the knot hole
roles.light: for the bleached ridges
roles.accent: for the scrap of blue rope

firstMark: Start with the longest crack in the wood, one wavering line of {dark}.
Start with the grain in long strokes of {main}, following the twist of the wood.

title: The Bladderwrack

doing.t: is dotted with air pockets just asking to be popped
is lying in a slick olive tangle
has a periwinkle clinging to one frond
is drying out, dark and leathery at the tips

close: Just one frond of bladderwrack, with its pairs of air pockets.
Only the bladderwrack, magnified, with a glint on each bubble.

roles.dark: for the shadows between the strands
roles.light: for the wet shine on each air pocket
roles.accent: for the amber where the light comes through

firstMark: Start with the air pockets: pairs of ovals in {main}, each with a bright spot of paper left on top.
Start with the midrib running up each frond in {dark}.

title: The Lavender

doing.t: is hanging upside down to dry
is tied round the middle with green string
is shedding purple grains at the slightest touch
has a bee clinging to every other spike

close: Just the bunch of lavender, stems bound together and flowers fanning out.
Only one stem of lavender, with its buds stacked up the spike.

roles.dark: for the deepest purple where the buds overlap
roles.light: for the silvery stems
roles.accent: for the string round the middle

firstMark: Start with the buds at the tip of one spike, stacked marks of {main}, like grains of rice.
Start with the darkest buds, low down on each spike, in short dabs of {dark}.

title: The Rose
phrases: a scent you lean in for

doing.t: is only half open, with a tight centre
is full blown and dropping its petals one by one
has a single drop of water sitting on one petal
is standing in a milk bottle, leaning to one side

close: Just the rose, looking straight down into the whorl of petals.
Only the rose and one leaf, from the side.

roles.dark: for the deep folds at the centre
roles.light: for the rolled edges where the light catches
roles.accent: for the green leaves and stem

firstMark: Start at the very centre with a tight curl of {dark}.
Start with the outer petal at the front in {main}, cupped like a hand.

title: The Sweet Peas

doing.t: are holding up their ruffled petals like flags
have one flower going over while the next bud opens
are crammed into a chipped mug, every colour at once
are scrambling up their canes

close: Just one sweet pea stem with three flowers, from bud to wide open.
Only one flower, up close, with its frilled top petal like a sail.

roles.main: for the pink and mauve petals
roles.dark: for the deepest colour at the heart of each flower
roles.light: for the paler frilled edges
roles.accent: for the curly green tendrils

firstMark: Start with the frilled edge of the top petal in {main}, a wavy line like the edge of a ribbon.
Start where the petals meet the stem, a tight knot of {dark}.

title: The Poppy

doing.t: has just shrugged off its bud case, petals still creased
is nodding on a long, wiry stem
has dropped its petals to show a pepper-pot seed head
has a bee dusted black with pollen in its middle

close: Just the poppy, looking into the black centre.
Only the seed head, with its flat, ridged crown on top.

roles.dark: for the black blotches and the centre
roles.light: for the creases where the light catches
roles.accent: for the grey-green stem and seed head

firstMark: Start with the black centre: a firm circle of {dark} with dots around it.
Start with the creases in the petals, light wavy lines of {main} running out from the middle.

title: The Catkins
phrases: the first yellow of the year

doing.t: are dangling like lambs' tails
are shaking out a puff of pollen
are still short, tight and green
are standing in a tall enamel jug with sprigs of pussy willow

close: Just the hazel twig with three catkins hanging from it.
Only one catkin, drawn large, with its overlapping scales.

roles.dark: for the twig
roles.light: for the dusting of pollen
roles.accent: for the red flowers along the twig

firstMark: Start with the twig, a crooked line of {dark} with a bud at each bend.
Start with one catkin as a column of overlapping scales in {main}.

title: The Horse Chestnut Leaf

doing.t: is spread out like a big green hand
is lying flat with all its leaflets fanned out
is still crumpled and limp, fresh from its sticky bud
is blotched with brown across its leaflets
has turned buttery yellow with rusty tips

close: Just the leaf, its leaflets spread from the stalk like fingers.
Only one leaflet, big enough to show each vein.

roles.dark: for the veins and the shadow where the leaflets meet
roles.light: for the lighter undersides
roles.accent: for the turning yellows and rusts

firstMark: Start where the leaflets meet the stalk, a star of {dark}.
Start with the midrib of the largest leaflet in {main}, then fan out the others.

title: The Apple Blossom

doing.t: has pink buds and open white flowers side by side
is losing petals at the slightest nudge
is all buds, still tight and pink
is standing in a pottery jug, already dropping petals

close: Just the sprig, five flowers and two leaves.
Only one apple flower, near enough to count the stamens.

roles.main: for the blush on the petals
roles.dark: for the twig
roles.light: for the white of the open flowers
roles.accent: for the yellow-tipped stamens and new leaves

firstMark: Start with the buds, rounded shapes of {main} pressed a little firmer than the open flowers.
Start with the twig in {dark}, gnarled where the flowers join it.

title: The Windfall Apple

doing.t: is rosy on one cheek and green on the other
still has one leaf hanging from its stalk
has a blackbird-pecked hollow in one side
is lying on its side to show the crinkled dimple underneath

close: Just the apple, with its stalk and the speckles on its skin.
Only the apple, cut in half to show the star of pips.

roles.dark: for the hollow round the stalk and the shadow underneath
roles.light: for the gloss along the curve
roles.accent: for the green side and the yellow freckles

firstMark: Start with the dip where the stalk goes in, a curl of {dark}.
Start with the red cheek in streaky strokes of {main} that follow the curve of the apple.

title: The Strawberry Plant

doing.t: has one berry ripe and the rest still white
is sending out a runner with a new plantlet dangling from it
has its best berry hidden right under the leaves
has white flowers with buttery middles

close: Just one strawberry, with its pips and the green ruff on top.
Only the strawberry plant, three leaves, one flower and one berry.

roles.dark: for the shadows under the leaves
roles.light: for the highlights on the berry and the white flowers
roles.accent: for the yellow pips

firstMark: Start with the dimples: a dot of {dark} beside each pip, then colour round them.
Start with the berry's outline in {main}, a fat heart shape with a rounded tip.

title: The Pea Pod
phrases: eaten before they reach the pan

doing.t: has been split open to show a row of peas
has one pea missing from the end of the row
is fat and bumpy, ready for picking
is still hanging on the plant beside a curly tendril

close: Just the pea pod, split open, with every pea a slightly different green.
Only the peas, lined up in their pod like passengers.

roles.dark: for the shadows between the peas
roles.light: for the shine on each pea
roles.accent: for the waxy inside of the pod

firstMark: Start with the peas: a row of circles in {main}, each with a dot of bare paper for the shine.
Start with the seam of the pod in a single line of {dark}.

title: The Radishes
phrases: pulled with the soil still on

doing.t: is still muddy at the roots
has been rinsed and is dripping clean
is tied with a twist of raffia, leaves flopping over

close: Just one radish, root and leaves and all.
Only the bunch, tied together, with the leaves drawn loosely.

roles.dark: for the soil and the shadow between the roots
roles.light: for the white tips and the shine
roles.accent: for the green leaves

firstMark: Start with one radish in {main}, round at the top and tapering to a white tail.
Start with the shadows where the radishes touch, slim wedges of {dark}.

title: The Allium
phrases: a lollipop on a long stick

doing.t: is a round purple globe of star-shaped flowers
sits high on a stalk as straight as a knitting needle
has a hoverfly resting on one of its stars
is splitting out of its papery bud skin
has dried to a sphere the colour of string

close: Just the allium head, a ball of flowers on its stem.
Only a handful of the flowers, enlarged, each one a six-pointed star.

roles.dark: for the shade at the back of the ball
roles.light: for the stars nearest the light
roles.accent: for the green stem

firstMark: Start with a light circle in {main} to place the ball, then fill it with star shapes.
Start with the shaded underside of the ball in {dark}, so the top can stay light.

title: The Daisy Chain
phrases: a crown for anyone sitting still

doing.t: is long enough to go round twice
has one daisy that keeps slipping out
is coiled up in a loose ring
has been finished off with a dandelion as the clasp

close: Just the daisy chain, curled in a loop, the flowers all facing up.
Only three links of the chain, near enough to see the slit in each stem.

roles.dark: for the shadow under the chain
roles.light: for the white of the petals

title: The Honesty

doing.t: is holding up its seed pods like a row of moons
has had its outer skins rubbed off to show the silver
still has three dark seeds showing through each pod
is standing on its own in an old glass bottle

close: Just one stem of honesty, five seed discs from big to small.
Only one seed pod, with the seeds showing through like shadows.

roles.dark: for the stalks and the seeds
roles.light: for the shine on each disc
roles.accent: for the faint violet at the edges

firstMark: Start with the seeds: three ovals of {dark} in each disc.
Start with the outline of the biggest disc in {main}, the lightest touch you have.

title: The Cobweb

doing.t: is sagging in the middle with the weight of its beads
is spun as round and neat as a dartboard
has its spider waiting patiently at the hub
has one broken thread trailing loose

close: Just the cobweb, with the threads left as bare white paper.
Only the middle of the web, near enough to see each bead.

roles.main: for the grey-blue shadows on the beads
roles.dark: for the background behind the web
roles.light: for the threads and the brightest beads
roles.accent: for the spider

firstMark: Start with the background: a dark layer of {dark} around the web, leaving the threads as bare paper.
Start with the spokes in faint, straight lines of {main}, from the middle outwards.

title: The Hyacinth
phrases: a scent that fills the hall

doing.t: is sending white roots down into the water
is leaning over, too heavy for its own stem
has a fat green bud nosing out of the top
is in full flower, every bell open

close: Just the hyacinth and its glass, with the roots coiling at the bottom.
Only the flower spike, its bells turned back at the tips.

roles.dark: for the deepest blue between the bells
roles.light: for the white roots and the shine on the glass
roles.accent: for the green leaves

firstMark: Start with the lowest bell of the flower spike in {main}, its petals turned back.
Start with the water line on the glass in {dark}, then leave the roots as bare paper beneath it.
